name: Anavar / oxandrolone voice risk

lead: Oxandrolone, known as Anavar, is an oral anabolic steroid once used medically for weight recovery and used by some for muscle and physique goals, including by women. This entry covers the voice effect: deepening is among its documented virilizing effects in women.

It is an androgen receptor agonist described as strongly anabolic with weak androgenic action, which is why women often choose it. Virilization still occurs, and its article states that such masculinizing changes, including voice deepening, can be irreversible. Voice change here is an off-target effect, not a studied goal.

paras: Women using it for physique purposes have often chosen it because it is described as more anabolic than androgenic. Non-medical use falls outside prescribing, and the voice effect is generally regarded as a risk rather than a goal.

Documented risks include voice deepening, hirsutism, menstrual changes, clitoral enlargement, liver damage, lipid changes, drug interactions and pregnancy contraindication. FDA approval was withdrawn in 2023, and it is a controlled substance.

angle.text: Oxandrolone is an oral anabolic steroid used for lean muscle and physique, and androgen action on the larynx can deepen the voice, particularly in women. Documented virilizing effects can be irreversible, and voice change is an off-target effect rather than a studied goal.

lead: Oxandrolone, sold as Oxandrin and widely known as Anavar or 'Var', is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid. In physique circles it is valued for lean-muscle gain and for use during fat-loss phases, and it has a reputation as one of the milder steroids, partly because it has strong anabolic and weak androgenic effects in rodent studies [1]. That reputation is the reason many women and first-time users have chosen it, and it is why its voice and virilization risks are a frequent topic.

Medically, it has been used to promote weight gain after surgery, trauma or chronic illness, to counter muscle loss from long-term corticosteroids, and to aid recovery from severe burns, where meta-analyses report more lean mass and faster donor-site healing [1][2]. Those same lean-mass effects are what bodybuilders and athletes seek for a harder, leaner physique [1][3].

In women, documented androgenic effects include voice deepening, body and facial hair growth, menstrual changes, male-pattern hair loss and clitoral enlargement, and the voice and other virilizing changes can be irreversible [1]. A 1989 survey of competitive bodybuilders in Kansas and Missouri found Anavar among the steroids reported by female competitors [4].
infobox: US Schedule III; Canada Schedule IV; UK Schedule 4 [1]

paras: Bodybuilders and athletes have used oxandrolone non-medically for muscle building, and it has appeared in professional doping cases [1]. It is popular with women and with people seeking milder steroid regimens, partly because of a reputation for lower liver toxicity [1]. A 1989 survey of competitive bodybuilders found it among the steroids named by both men and women, with the main reason for steroid use being the perception that they helped win competitions [4].

Labeled and off-label uses include weight gain after surgery, trauma, chronic infection or HIV wasting, countering corticosteroid-related muscle breakdown, and bone pain in osteoporosis [1]. A 2022 systematic review of six randomized trials found a skin-healing advantage with oxandrolone as an adjunct in adult burn patients and no benefit in pressure ulcers [2]. A 2019 Cochrane review, as described on Wikipedia, found moderate-quality evidence that adding it to growth hormone increased adult height in girls with Turner syndrome [1].

Reported masculinizing effects in women include voice deepening, body and facial hair growth, menstrual irregularity, male-pattern hair loss and clitoral enlargement, and these can persist after use stops [1]. Clinically, doses for women and children are kept low and patients are monitored [1].

Liver enzymes can rise, especially at high doses or prolonged use, and peliosis hepatis, liver failure and liver tumors have been documented; the early belief that it was far less liver-toxic than other oral steroids did not hold up [1]. It alters blood lipids, can reduce male fertility, strongly potentiates warfarin and is contraindicated in pregnancy [1]. A 2020 case report described delayed rhabdomyolysis after a man used Anavar for 60 consecutive days [5].

Oxandrolone is a 17-alpha-methylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone with an oxygen atom replacing carbon 2. It is an androgen receptor agonist with strong anabolic and weak androgenic effects in rodents, is about 97% absorbed orally and does not convert to estrogens, so gynecomastia is generally not expected [1].

Searle researchers described oxandrolone in 1962 and it entered US medical use in 1964. Searle discontinued Anavar in 1989, partly because of publicity about illicit bodybuilding use, and Savient launched Oxandrin in 1995. A 1984 FDA advisory committee had found no evidence of efficacy. The manufacturer requested withdrawal in 2019, the FDA moved to remove it in December 2022 and formally withdrew approval in June 2023 [1].

Looksmax.org has threads on Anavar for cutting and for height. One poster planning use in his mid-teens cites pediatric growth studies and says he wants to address a delayed bone age [6]. Other posters in those discussions say it affects natural hormone production and should not be run alone [6]. Another thread describes it as great for cutting [7]. This site does not give dosing or sourcing guidance.
No studies found on oxandrolone and voice change in women specifically. Studies of the drug cover burns [2], pressure ulcers [2] and Turner syndrome [1].
